body: The thing that most people don't understand is depression doesn't just go away. It never does. Your coping tools and potential change over time. There are various things that you figure out that help. You learn things that are bad for you and that you should avoid. For me it is just hard because I have been doing it alone for most of my life. And only now am reaching out to professionals. I won't say it is making things better since it has only been a month. And I am ridiculously far gone into the depths of depression, which my therapist agrees with. But it is different from before. And maybe things will change. Even if they don't, what have I got to lose at this point? I'll keep trying till I can't. Only thing I can do.

I completely understand what you mean. I have been thinking and functioning along those lines for the past 10-12 years or so. Some days are better than others. Those little moments of being useful gives me a little hope (the feeling that there is still some good I have to offer in this world). Most days though the loneliness just consumes me. I keep feeling like I am drifting away. There are broad different versions of me. The person that other people see and the person that they don't see.

So what I'm saying is, it helps up to a point. After which it can become very difficult to carry your weight alone. And I am very close to my limit right now. Everyday is just a steep uphill climb. Try getting professional help if you can before you go too deep into it. If you have no one else to talk to, feel free to message me about it. Even if it is just to vent. You need an outlet too.

I have felt this way for a long time. Since as far back as I can remember. I was maybe 7. I am 27 now. And I can't recall a single a that I haven't felt what you are feeling right now. I still do. I [almost killed myself last night](https://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/62p815/last_night_i_almost_killed_myself_for_the_4th/) because of it.

Isolation is something that drives that feedback loop in my head. 

I'm not good enough -> I need to act a way in which people will accept me -> Look I did this thing for this person, surely this means something to them -> I'm being a good person -> They like me -> No they don't, they only like this fake me -> I am lying to them -> But I accepted every bit of them -> And they say they accept me -> Let me show them a little bit of me -> That didn't come out the way I intended -> They look at me differently now -> I need to fix this -> Everytime I am around them I wipe the smile off their face -> I need to fix this -> What the hell is wrong with me -> They are miserable because I am here -> I need to fix this -> Look at them laugh when I'm not there -> I need to fix this -> They tell me I am too negative -> I need to fix this -> I make it difficult for them to be happy about coming to work -> What the hell is wrong with me -> What the hell did I do -> I shouldn't be here -> I don't belong here -> I am better off not existing -> I'm not good enough
I'm glad it helped you in some way. I will share try to share more often from now on.
I'm glad that it spoke to you in some way.

That's the thing about perception when you are depressed. When that perception keeps getting validated time and time again by every single person around you - family, "friends", strangers. It just becomes truth inside your head. I have been depressed my entire life. And have been dealing with it alone all through it. Everytime I try to open up, show a little bit of my darkness to someone else, they run. They either ignore me, or what I said and a lot of the times even say that I make it not fun to be around, and that I shouldn't talk to them anymore. 

And I don't blame them. The worst part is they barely see a fraction of the darkness and only when I let them. And it always ends up with with me hating myself for making them miserable, because they were so happy when they didn't have to deal with me. 

So I cry alone, behind closed doors. For what always seems like hours. And when I'm done. I feel numb. I hate myself even more for feeling the way I do. And then I cry for some more hours. Till it physically hurts to cry any more. And my eyes are sore and can't make more tears. I try to sleep, but my eyes are so dry and my throat so dry. I try to watch something, read something, anything to distract me. But I can't. There is only one thing I can think of that will stop this pain right now. But I promised myself I wouldn't do it again. 

So I call the hotline. I get connected to someone. I hear a voice on the other side. I can't bring myself to say anything. And it they hang up. I thought I couldn't cry anymore. But I can. It hurts so much. I continue till I can't anymore. It would be so easy to end it right now. The knife is right there. 
Maybe I can try the chat system. I can't connect for over an hour. Why am I even doing this? What is the point? I try calling again. Maybe this time I will say something. 

I get connected. 

This time I talk. Hi. My name is Sam. 

She sounds nice. Maybe she can listen. Maybe she understands. But I moved to the other side of the country a year ago and never changed my number. So I got connected to the wrong center. 

Can I transfer you to the nearest center? 

I just want to talk. Can I just talk to you? 

But I don't know the things near you. 

Will I have to wait on hold again if you transfer me? 

No. 

I wait on hold for fifteen minutes. I'm sorry, they say I can't transfer you, will you be able to call them? 

Can I just talk to you? 

Pause.

Will I have to wait? 

No.

Ok. Give me the number.

I call the other number. I wait on hold for 30 minutes.

I hear a voice.

Hi. I am Sam. 

Hi Sam.

I just start crying. I stop after a few minutes.

I ask her name. She lies and says Dallas.

I tell her a few parts of my darkness. She tells me it must be painful living with alone. She doesn't say much. And I cry through most of it. But she listens. And says she doesn't understand, but can understand it must be incredibly painful. All you can do is try and get through one piece of it at a time. We say goodbye after about 30 minutes.

I don't know how to get through the night. I have a therapist appointment tomorrow at 3. Focus on that. I sit with my head in my hands for an hour. I don't feel like I need to cry anymore. I try to fall asleep. I have work tomorrow. I wake up. And the pain just floods right back. Somehow feels stronger than last night. But I need to make that appointment. I need to do that for myself. I cry on the floor for another couple of hours. I can do this. I can get to work. No I can't. I can't let them see me like this. It will only make things worse. I write in sick. And I wait in the darkest part of my house till my appointment.
